title: ws/mod.rs parse_ws_frame: String allocation for type_name before match — borrow instead
description: ws/mod.rs lines 123-127: type_name is allocated as a String with .to_string() so it can be passed to WsFrame::Unknown if needed. The match on line 129 then calls type_name.as_str() to borrow it back for pattern matching. This is correct but slightly awkward — the allocation is only unconditionally needed if the frame is Unknown. A cleaner pattern: let type_str = ...; match type_str { "StateChange" => ..., "Response" => ..., other => Ok(WsFrame::Unknown { type_name: other.to_owned() }) }. The current code is not wrong, but a Rust practitioner would notice the allocate-then-borrow-back dance.
